content: 1. Administer 5 mg/kg intravenously every 12 hours for a minimum of 7 days. Refer to the administration guidelines for IV preparation and infusion rates. 2. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases amiodarone levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 4. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib and refer to the drug monograph for dosage modifications. 5. Quinupristin/dalfopristin reduces the efficacy of live BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administer live bacterial vaccines only after completing antibiotic therapy. 6. Quinupristin/dalfopristin reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 7. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases clarithromycin levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 8. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (including intranasal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases dronedarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases encorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose by half. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 12. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases entrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose of entrectinib after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 13. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases ergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 15. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases finerenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, and adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 17. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases haloperidol levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 18. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily for B-cell malignancies or 420 mg daily for graft-versus-host disease. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 19. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases infigratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases lovastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases lurbinectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Quinupristin/dalfopristin reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 24. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases intranasal midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation due to higher systemic exposure. 25. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases neratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nirogacestat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg daily and monitor closely for adverse effects. Further reduce to 50 mg daily if adverse effects emerge. 28. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases pacritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases pazopanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg daily. 30. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases pemigatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 31. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases pexidartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 32. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases pimozide levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 33. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases red yeast rice levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is identical to lovastatin, and may increase creatine kinase levels, leading to a higher risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 35. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and wait 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 36. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose as per the monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 37. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 40. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per the drug monograph. 42. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Quinupristin/dalfopristin reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administer live bacterial vaccines only after completing antibiotic therapy. 44. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%; reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 45. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases acalabrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 46. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases almotriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases alprazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases amiodarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases aprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases artemether/lumefantrine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases avanafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and associated adverse events. Limit the maximum dose of avanafil to 50 mg, not exceeding once every 24 hours, for patients taking moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Quinupristin/dalfopristin decreases the efficacy of oral forms of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This has a low risk of contraceptive failure. 56. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases buprenorphine subdermal implant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication if CYP3A4 inhibitors are newly initiated. If the dose of the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary.
